title: Si Bien: Granting a True Point

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *si bien* from B2 Unit 8: a formal way to say "although it is true that", followed by the indicative. It lets you grant a point about the pampa or the gaucho and then say what matters more.

sections.title: Si bien at work on the pampa
rows: Si bien la pampa parece plana, tiene paisajes muy variados.
*si bien* + indicative: it is true that it looks flat
Si bien el gaucho fue una figura real, su imagen es en parte un mito.
the first clause grants a fact; the second says what you want to stress
La vida del campo, si bien cambió mucho, conserva tradiciones.
Si bien trabajaban con el ganado, muchos gauchos eran peones.
also in the past, with the indicative

items.spanish: Si bien la pampa parece plana, tiene paisajes muy variados.
items.english: Although the pampa looks flat, it has very varied landscapes.

items.spanish: Si bien el gaucho fue una figura real, su imagen es en parte un mito.
items.english: Although the gaucho was a real figure, his image is partly a myth.

items.spanish: La vida del campo, si bien cambió mucho, conserva sus tradiciones.
items.english: Country life, although it changed a lot, keeps its traditions.

items.spanish: Si bien trabajaban con el ganado, muchos gauchos eran peones.
items.english: Although they worked with cattle, many gauchos were farmhands.

sections.content: *Si bien* is formal and takes the indicative here, with no *que* after it. In everyday speech, say *aunque*. Do not confuse *si bien* with *sí* ("yes").
